history.hpi: Wife noticed sudden onset of right facial droop, right arm weakness, and inability to speak clearly approximately 45 minutes prior to EMS arrival while eating breakfast. Patient was last seen speaking normally at the start of breakfast, roughly 45 minutes ago. No witnessed trauma, no seizure activity, no head strike.
history.lastOralIntake: A few bites of toast and coffee approximately 20 minutes prior to symptom onset
history.events: Wife called 911 immediately after noticing facial droop and absent speech during breakfast

scene.location: Single-family home, kitchen table, patient seated in chair
scene.bystanders: Wife present, witnessed onset, provides last known well time
visualCues: Right arm drifts and falls when raised
Patient attempting to speak but unable to form words
Apixaban pill bottle visible on counter

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 72-year-old male seated at the kitchen table with obvious right facial droop and right arm weakness. He is alert but unable to produce clear speech. Wife reports normal function 45 minutes ago.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent, mild pooling of saliva on right side of mouth
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, irregularly irregular rhythm palpated
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Right arm and leg weakness, drifts and falls when raised against gravity; left-sided strength intact
otherFindings: Expressive aphasia — unable to produce clear words
Follows simple commands with left hand
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: (Attempts to speak, produces only garbled sounds)

transitions.condition: Crew performs a validated prehospital stroke scale, establishes a specific last known well time from the wife, and checks blood glucose to exclude hypoglycemia as a stroke mimic.

phases.name: Stroke scale and LKW obtained
phases.description: Crew completes a focused stroke assessment: positive facial droop, right arm drift, and absent speech consistent with a positive stroke scale. LKW time is confirmed as 45 minutes ago. BGL is checked and is normal, ruling out hypoglycemia as the cause.
phases.triggerCondition: After the primary survey confirms no immediate life threats, the crew performs a validated stroke scale (facial droop, arm drift, speech), confirms last known well time from the wife, and checks blood glucose to exclude hypoglycemia as a stroke mimic.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, irregularly irregular rhythm
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Right arm and leg weakness persists; left-sided strength intact
otherFindings: Stroke scale positive: facial droop + arm drift + speech deficit
LKW confirmed as 45 minutes ago per wife

expectedActions.shortAction: Check blood glucose; treat only if BGL less than 60 mg/dL
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Check blood glucose level (BGL) Treat only if glucose less than 60 mg/dL
expectedActions.rationale: Hypoglycemia is a common, rapidly reversible stroke mimic that must be excluded.

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform validated stroke scale and severity scale (face, arm, speech)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Use a validated prehospital stroke scale that may include, but is not limited to: Facial smile/grimace – ask patient to smile; Arm drift – close eyes and hold out arms for count of 10 seconds; Speech – ask patient to say "You can't teach an old dog new tricks"
expectedActions.rationale: A validated scale standardizes findings and drives the destination decision.

expectedActions.shortAction: Determine and document a specific last known well time from bystander
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Determine "last known well" time "Last known well" must be specific
expectedActions.rationale: A specific LKW time determines eligibility for thrombolytic and thrombectomy therapy at the receiving hospital.

expectedActions.shortAction: Administer oxygen only as needed to target 94–98% SpO2
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer oxygen as appropriate with a target of achieving 94–98% saturation
expectedActions.rationale: Routine high-flow O2 is not indicated when saturation is already adequate.

expectedActions.shortAction: Elevate head of stretcher 15–30°; keep head and neck neutral
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Prevent aspiration – elevate head of stretcher 15–30 degrees if systolic BP greater than 100 mmHg Maintain head and neck in neutral alignment, without flexing the neck
expectedActions.rationale: Positioning reduces aspiration risk in a patient with impaired airway protection.

expectedActions.shortAction: Acquire 12-lead EKG and place patient on cardiac monitor
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Acquire 12-lead EKG, if possible Place on cardiac monitor
expectedActions.rationale: Identifies atrial fibrillation or other dysrhythmia as a possible embolic source.

transitions.condition: With a positive stroke scale and LKW within the thrombolytic window, the crew transmits an early stroke alert to the receiving hospital including LVO suspicion, and transports without delay while avoiding treatment of hypertension.
Crew fails to obtain a specific last known well time from the wife, complicating the receiving hospital's eligibility determination for thrombolytic or thrombectomy therapy.

phases.name: Stroke alert transmitted, transport initiated
phases.description: Patient is packaged and transported to an appropriate stroke center given the severity of findings and LKW within the thrombolytic and thrombectomy treatment windows. Hospital notified early with a stroke alert including LVO suspicion.
phases.triggerCondition: With a positive stroke scale, confirmed LKW at 45 minutes, and glucose ruled out as a mimic, the crew transmits an early stroke alert to the receiving hospital — including LVO suspicion given the severity findings — and initiates transport without delay, avoiding treatment of the patient's hypertension per protocol.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, irregularly irregular rhythm
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Right arm and leg weakness unchanged; left-sided strength intact
otherFindings: Persistent right facial droop, arm weakness, and aphasia unchanged
Head of stretcher elevated 30°, neck neutral

expectedActions.shortAction: Transmit early stroke alert to receiving hospital including LVO suspicion
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Early hospital notification per local stroke plan that should include any suspected large vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke
expectedActions.rationale: Early notification activates the hospital stroke team before arrival, minimizing door-to-treatment time.

expectedActions.shortAction: Do not treat hypertension; monitor without pharmacologic intervention
expectedActions.rationale: Elevated BP may be a compensatory response maintaining cerebral perfusion; lowering it can worsen ischemia.

phases.name: LKW time not established
phases.description: Without a precise LKW time, the hospital stroke team cannot confirm whether the patient falls within the thrombolytic or thrombectomy treatment windows, potentially delaying or excluding him from time-sensitive interventions.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew fails to obtain a specific last known well time from the wife, documenting only "found this morning," which complicates the receiving hospital's eligibility determination for thrombolytic or thrombectomy therapy.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, irregularly irregular rhythm
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Right arm and leg weakness persists; left-sided strength intact
otherFindings: Wife's last known well time recorded only as "sometime this morning"
Stroke scale still positive: facial droop + arm drift + speech deficit
Receiving hospital unable to confirm thrombolytic eligibility window on arrival

expectedActions.shortAction: Re-question bystanders to pin down a specific, defensible LKW time before arrival
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: "Last known well" must be specific If the patient was last known well prior to bedtime the night before, this is the time to be documented (not time the patient woke up with symptoms present)
expectedActions.rationale: A vague LKW time can wrongly exclude a treatable patient from time-sensitive stroke therapies.
